title.zh: 卷394 列傳一百八十一 徐广缙 葉名琛 黄宗汉
title.en: Volume 394 Biographies 181: Xu Guangjin, Ye Mingchen, Huang Zonghan
title.raw: 卷394 列傳一百八十一 徐广缙 葉名琛 黄宗汉

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十一

translations.literal: Biographies 181
translations.idiomatic: Biography 181

sentences.zh: 徐廣縉葉名琛黃宗漢

translations.literal: Xu Guangjin, Ye Mingchen, Huang Zonghan
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangjin, Ye Mingchen, and Huang Zonghan

sentences.zh: 徐廣縉，字仲升，河南鹿邑人。

translations.literal: Xu Guangjin, courtesy name Zhongsheng, was a native of Luyi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangjin, whose courtesy name was Zhongsheng, came from Luyi in Henan Province.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, appointed reviser, and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-fifth year of the Jiaqing reign (1820), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary academician, was appointed revising compiler, and later became a censor.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，出為陝西榆林知府，歷安徽徽寧池太道、江西督糧道、福建按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Yulin in Shaanxi, and successively served as intendant of Huining, Chizhou, and Taiping in Anhui, grain transport commissioner of Jiangxi, and provincial judicial commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang (1833) he was posted as prefect of Yulin in Shaanxi, then served in turn as intendant of the Huining–Chizhou–Taiping circuit in Anhui, Jiangxi grain transport commissioner, and Fujian provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 擢順天府尹，尋出為四川布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Shuntian Prefecture, and soon after sent out as provincial treasurer of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of the capital prefecture of Shuntian, and shortly afterward was appointed provincial treasurer of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，補江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was assigned as provincial treasurer of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he left office for mourning; when the mourning period ended, he was appointed provincial treasurer of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢雲南巡撫，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Daoguang (1846) he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and then transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢兩廣總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi, concurrently serving as superintendent of trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1848) he was promoted to governor-general of the two Guang provinces and concurrently appointed superintendent of foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 自江寧定約五口通商，許廣州省城設立棧房，領事入城，以平禮相待。

translations.literal: Since the Treaty of Nanjing opened five ports to trade, Canton was permitted to establish warehouses in the provincial city and consuls were allowed to enter the city and be received with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Treaty of Nanjing, which opened five treaty ports, Canton had been allowed to set up bonded warehouses in the provincial city and foreign consuls were to enter the city and be received on equal terms.

sentences.zh: 粵民堅執洋人不准入城舊制，聚眾以抗，官不能解。

translations.literal: The people of Guangdong firmly upheld the old rule that foreigners must not enter the city, gathered in crowds to resist, and the officials could not resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: The Cantonese clung to the old prohibition on foreigners entering the city, rallied in crowds to resist, and the authorities could not settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 總督耆英既與英人議緩俟二年之後，尋內召，廣縉繼任。

translations.literal: Governor-General Qishan had already agreed with the English to defer the matter for two years; soon he was recalled to the capital, and Guangjin succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Qishan had already negotiated with the British to postpone entry for two years; he was soon recalled to the capital, and Guangjin took his place.

sentences.zh: 會黃竹岐鄉民毆殺英人六，領事德庇時要挾賠償保護，廣縉治殺人者罪，而拒其非理之求，戒諭人民毋暴動，事得解。

translations.literal: It happened that villagers of Huangzhuqi beat to death six Englishmen; Consul Davis demanded compensation and protection by coercion; Guangjin punished the killers but refused his unreasonable demands, admonished the people not to riot, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers at Huangzhuqi killed six Britons in a beating, Consul Davis pressed for compensation and guarantees; Guangjin punished the killers but refused his unreasonable demands, warned the populace against violence, and the incident was closed.

sentences.zh: 德庇時回國，文翰代為領事，初至請謁。

translations.literal: Davis returned to his country; Bonham replaced him as consul and on first arrival requested an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Davis went home, Bonham became consul in his stead and on arrival asked for an official audience.

sentences.zh: 廣縉赴虎門閱砲台，延見之，遂登其舟，示以坦白。

translations.literal: Guangjin went to Humen to inspect the batteries, received him in audience, then boarded his vessel to show frankness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin went to Humen to inspect the forts, received him there, and even boarded his ship to show openness and good faith.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，文翰以兩年入城之期已屆，要踐約，廣縉諭以耆英所許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Bonham said the two-year period for entering the city had arrived and demanded fulfillment of the agreement; Guangjin instructed him regarding what Qishan had promised.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1849) Bonham argued that the two-year deferral had expired and demanded that the agreement be honored; Guangjin cited the terms Qishan had granted.

sentences.zh: 乃姑為權宜之計，民情憤激，眾怒難犯，非官所能禁止。

translations.literal: He then made a temporary expedient: popular sentiment was inflamed, the wrath of the masses was not to be provoked, and officials could not restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a provisional compromise: the people were furious, public anger could not be defied, and the government could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 文翰則堅持成約，且以他省入城相詰難，揚言將駕兵船至天津訴諸京師，相持不下。

translations.literal: Bonham insisted on the established agreement, moreover challenged by citing entry into cities in other provinces, and declared he would sail warships to Tianjin to appeal to the capital; the standoff could not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Bonham held firm to the treaty, countered by pointing to foreign access in other provinces, and threatened to send warships to Tianjin to lodge a complaint in the capital; neither side would yield.

sentences.zh: 廣縉疏聞，自請嚴議。

translations.literal: Guangjin memorialized the throne and asked that he be severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin reported the situation to the throne and asked to be held strictly accountable.

sentences.zh: 密詔許暫入城一次，以踐前言，不得習以為常。

translations.literal: A secret edict permitted one temporary entry into the city to fulfill the earlier promise, but it must not become customary.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict allowed a single temporary entry to honor the earlier pledge, on condition that it not become routine.

sentences.zh: 廣縉复疏言：「入城萬不可行。

translations.literal: Guangjin memorialized again, saying: "Entry into the city is absolutely impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin memorialized again: "Allowing entry into the city is utterly out of the question.

sentences.zh: 廣東民情剽悍，與閩、浙、江蘇不同。

translations.literal: The temperament of the people of Guangdong is fierce, unlike Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong are far fiercer than those of Fujian, Zhejiang, or Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 阻其入城而有事，則眾志成城，尚有爪牙之可恃；

translations.literal: If we block their entry and trouble arises, then united wills make a strong city and we still have forces to rely on;
translations.idiomatic: If we keep them out and trouble follows, the people will stand as one and we will still have forces we can count on;

sentences.zh: 許其入城而有事，則人心瓦解，必至內外之交訌。

translations.literal: if we permit their entry and trouble arises, then hearts will disintegrate and internal and external conflict will surely ensue.
translations.idiomatic: but if we let them in and trouble follows, morale will collapse and we will face rebellion within and without.

sentences.zh: 明知有害無利，詎敢輕於一試。」

translations.literal: Knowing clearly it is harmful without benefit, how dare one lightly try it."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing full well that the harm outweighs any gain, how could I dare experiment lightly?"

sentences.zh: 卒堅拒之。

translations.literal: In the end he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he stood firm and refused.

sentences.zh: 英人乃集兵船三於香港，​​放小艇至海口各港測水探路，示恫喝。

translations.literal: The English then assembled three warships at Hong Kong, sent small boats to various ports at the sea mouths to sound depths and explore routes, showing intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: The British then concentrated three warships at Hong Kong and sent launches to sound the harbors along the coast as a show of force.

sentences.zh: 廣縉增兵守諸砲台及要隘，嚴備以待。

translations.literal: Guangjin increased troops to guard the batteries and strategic passes, making strict preparations to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin reinforced the forts and key passes and made ready for whatever might come.

sentences.zh: 時民團號十萬，聲勢甚張。

translations.literal: At the time the militia claimed one hundred thousand men, and their momentum was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia at the time claimed a strength of one hundred thousand, and their presence was formidable.

sentences.zh: 華商會議暫停各國貿易，密告美、法兩國領事，啟釁實由英人。

translations.literal: Chinese merchants met and resolved to suspend trade with all nations, secretly informing the American and French consuls that the provocation came from the English.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants agreed to suspend trade with all foreign powers and quietly told the American and French consuls that the British had provoked the crisis.

sentences.zh: 於是諸洋商慮受擾累，將以損失歸領事負責。

translations.literal: Thereupon the foreign merchants feared suffering disturbance and loss, and would hold the consul responsible for damages.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign traders then feared they would bear the cost of the disruption and looked to their consuls to answer for the losses.

sentences.zh: 士紳聯名致文翰，為反覆陳利害甚切。

translations.literal: Gentry and scholars jointly addressed Bonham, repeatedly setting forth the advantages and harms with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry sent Bonham a joint petition, pressing him again and again on the stakes involved.

sentences.zh: 文翰內受牽制，乃罷入城之議，乞照舊通商。

translations.literal: Bonham, constrained within, then abandoned the entry proposal and begged to trade as before.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between pressures, Bonham dropped the demand for entry and asked only that trade resume as before.

sentences.zh: 與要約，停市開巿皆非由官令，不進城即通商，後有反覆，仍行停止。

translations.literal: They made a compact: stopping or opening the market were not by official order; without entering the city trade would proceed; if there were reversal later, stopping would still be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed that neither closing nor reopening the market would be by official decree; trade would continue without entry into the city, and any later breach would bring a renewed boycott.

sentences.zh: 事既定，廣縉疏聞，宣宗大悅。

translations.literal: When the matter was settled, Guangjin memorialized; the Xuanzong Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was settled, Guangjin reported to the throne, and the Daoguang Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「洋務之興，將十年矣。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Foreign affairs have arisen for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Foreign relations have troubled us for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 沿海擾累，糜餉勞師，近雖略臻安謐，而馭之之法，剛柔未得其平，流弊因而愈出。

translations.literal: The coast has been disturbed and burdened, funds wasted and armies wearied; though recently there has been some quiet, the methods of control have not balanced firmness and yielding, and abuses have therefore increased.
translations.idiomatic: The coastlands have been harried, treasure spent, and troops worn down; though things have lately grown somewhat calmer, we have not struck the right balance between firmness and concession, and new abuses keep appearing.

sentences.zh: 朕恐瀕海居民或遭蹂躪，一切隱忍待之。

translations.literal: We feared that coastal residents might suffer ravages, and bore everything in forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing harm to our coastal people, We have endured much in silence.

sentences.zh: 昨英酋复伸入城之請，徐廣縉等悉心措理，動合機宜。

translations.literal: Yesterday the English chief again pressed the request to enter the city; Xu Guangjin and others handled it with full care, every move fitting the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When the British envoy again demanded entry into the city, Xu Guangjin and his colleagues handled the matter with care, and their measures were well judged throughout.

sentences.zh: 入城議寢，依舊通商。

translations.literal: The entry proposal was laid to rest; trade continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The entry question was dropped, and trade went on as before.

sentences.zh: 不折一兵，不發一矢，中外綏靖，可以久安，實深嘉悅！」

translations.literal: Not a soldier was broken, not an arrow loosed; China and foreigners were pacified and long peace could be secured—We are deeply gratified!"
translations.idiomatic: Not a man was lost, not an arrow fired; peace was restored at home and abroad, and lasting calm seems possible—We are deeply pleased!"

sentences.zh: 於是錫封廣縉一等子爵，賜雙眼花翎，是役商民一心，尤得紳士許祥光、伍崇曜之力為多，二人並被優擢。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangjin was enfeoffed as a first-rank baron, granted double-eyed peacock feathers; in this campaign merchants and people were of one mind, especially aided by gentry Xu Xiangguang and Wu Chongyao, and both were specially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin was then created a first-class baron and granted the double-eyed peacock feather. In this affair merchants and commoners stood together, with particular help from the gentrymen Xu Xiangguang and Wu Chongyao, both of whom received exceptional promotions.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，文翰復言國王以進城未能如約，為人所輕，似覺赧顏，請為轉奏，廣縉以罷議進城之後貿易始復，豈可再申前說，拒之。

translations.literal: After several months Bonham again said the king, because entry could not be fulfilled as agreed, was held in contempt and seemed ashamed, and asked that it be relayed to the throne; Guangjin said that only after abandoning entry had trade resumed—how could the former proposal be raised again—and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Bonham wrote that his king felt humiliated because entry had not been granted as promised and asked that the matter be referred to Beijing; Guangjin replied that trade had resumed only after the entry demand was dropped and refused to reopen the question.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文翰又遺書大學士穆彰阿、耆英，遣人至上海、天津投遞。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Bonham again sent letters to Grand Secretary Mujangga and Qishan, dispatching men to deliver them at Shanghai and Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1850) Bonham again wrote to Grand Secretaries Mujangga and Qishan and sent couriers to deliver the letters at Shanghai and Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 文翰尋自赴上海，欲有所陳請，先後卻之；

translations.literal: Bonham soon went in person to Shanghai wishing to present petitions, but was repeatedly turned away;
translations.idiomatic: Bonham soon went to Shanghai in person hoping to lodge petitions, but was turned away each time;

sentences.zh: 乃回香港，蓋覬覦未已也。

translations.literal: he then returned to Hong Kong—for his covetous designs had not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: he then returned to Hong Kong, his designs evidently not yet abandoned.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣盜賊蜂起，以廣西金田洪秀全為最悍。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere in the two Guang provinces; Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guangxi was the fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising throughout the two Guang provinces, and the fiercest leader was Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭祖琛柔懦縱賊，廣縉疏劾其養筴貽患，罷之。

translations.literal: Governor Zheng Zuchen was weak and indulgent toward bandits; Guangjin memorialized impeaching him for nurturing trouble and causing harm, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zheng Zuchen was timid and let the rebels grow; Guangjin impeached him for indulging the threat and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 廣東韶州、廉州匪亦蔓延，廣縉遣軍扼梧州、肇慶。

translations.literal: Bandits in Shaozhou and Qinzhou of Guangdong also spread; Guangjin sent troops to hold Wuzhou and Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels also spread through Shaozhou and Qinzhou in Guangdong, and Guangjin sent troops to block them at Wuzhou and Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 詔廣縉赴廣西剿辦，尋起林則徐督師，命廣縉剿捕廣東遊匪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guangjin to go to Guangxi to suppress and handle matters; soon Lin Zexu was recalled to command the army, and Guangjin was ordered to pursue and capture roving bandits in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Guangjin to Guangxi to suppress the rebels; Lin Zexu was soon recalled to take command, and Guangjin was told to clear the roving bandits of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，出駐高州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he went out to station at Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) he took the field and established headquarters at Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 匪首凌十八、陳二、吳三、何茗科踞羅鏡圩及信宜，與洪秀全聲勢相倚。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs Ling Shiba, Chen Er, Wu San, and He Mingke occupied Luojing Market and Xinyi, their momentum leaning on Hong Xiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders Ling Shiba, Chen Er, Wu San, and He Mingke held Luojing Market and Xinyi, coordinating their strength with Hong Xiuquan.

sentences.zh: 廣縉遣兵進擊，殲吳三，追何茗科至貴縣擒之；

translations.literal: Guangjin sent troops to attack, annihilated Wu San, pursued He Mingke to Guixian and captured him;
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin sent troops against them, destroyed Wu San's force, pursued He Mingke to Guixian and captured him;

sentences.zh: 又破廉州賊顏品瑤，擒李士青。

translations.literal: he also defeated the Qinzhou bandit Yan Pinyao and captured Li Shiqing.
translations.idiomatic: he also defeated the Qinzhou rebel Yan Pinyao and took Li Shiqing prisoner.

sentences.zh: 二年春，乘勝進攻羅鏡圩，擒凌十八。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, pressing the victory he attacked Luojing Market and captured Ling Shiba.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year (1852) he pressed the advantage, stormed Luojing Market, and captured Ling Shiba.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was given the honorary title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On news of the victory he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 命馳赴梧州，而洪秀全大股已犯桂林，竄入湖南。

translations.literal: He was ordered to hurry to Wuzhou, but Hong Xiuquan's main force had already attacked Guilin and fled into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to rush to Wuzhou, but Hong Xiuquan's main column had already struck Guilin and slipped into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿以罪黜，授廣縉欽差大臣，署理湖廣總督。

translations.literal: Saišangga was dismissed for his crimes; Guangjin was appointed imperial commissioner and acting governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Saišangga was disgraced and removed; Guangjin was made imperial commissioner and acting governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十月，至衡州，賊攻長沙甚急，駱秉章、張亮基力守，屢挫賊，乃下竄岳州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Hengzhou; the rebels pressed Changsha fiercely; Luo Bingzhang and Zhang Liangji defended strenuously, repeatedly defeating the rebels, who then fled down to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Hengzhou. The rebels were pressing Changsha hard; Luo Bingzhang and Zhang Liangji held the city and beat them back repeatedly, and the rebels finally broke south toward Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 廣縉始抵長沙。

translations.literal: Guangjin only then reached Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin arrived at Changsha only after the crisis had passed.

sentences.zh: 未幾。

translations.literal: Before long.
translations.idiomatic: Before long,

sentences.zh: 岳州亦陷，直犯武昌。

translations.literal: Yuezhou also fell, and they pressed straight on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou fell as well, and the rebels drove straight on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廣縉進駐岳州，而漢陽、武昌相繼陷。

translations.literal: Guangjin advanced to station at Yuezhou, but Hanyang and Wuchang fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin moved up to Yuezhou, yet Hanyang and Wuchang fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 詔斥廣縉遷延不進，調度失機，株守岳州，擁兵自眾，褫職逮問，籍其家，論大辟。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Guangjin for delay in advancing, loss of opportunity in command, clinging to Yuezhou, amassing troops for his own display; his office was stripped, he was arrested for trial, his property confiscated, and death was decreed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Guangjin for slow advance, missed chances, holding uselessly at Yuezhou, and keeping a large force under his personal control; he was dismissed, arrested, his property seized, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，粵匪入河南境，釋廣縉，交巡撫陸應穀差遣，責令帶罪自效。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year Guangdong rebels entered Henan; Guangjin was released, handed to Governor Lu Yinggu for assignment, and ordered to redeem his guilt by service.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year (1853), when Guangdong rebels entered Henan, Guangjin was freed, placed at the disposal of Governor Lu Yinggu, and ordered to win back his honor through service.

sentences.zh: 率兵駐歸德，防剿捻匪有功。

translations.literal: Leading troops he stationed at Guide, defending and suppressing Nian bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to Guide, where he helped guard against and suppress the Nian rebels with distinction.

sentences.zh: 八年，命赴勝保軍營，尋予四品卿銜，留鳳陽從袁甲三剿捻匪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to Sheng Bao's camp; soon given fourth-rank ministerial rank, he remained at Fengyang following Yuan Jiasan in suppressing Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1858) he was sent to Sheng Bao's headquarters; he soon received fourth-rank ministerial rank and stayed at Fengyang to campaign against the Nian under Yuan Jiasan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 葉名琛，字昆臣，湖北漢陽人。

translations.literal: Ye Mingchen, courtesy name Kunchen, was a native of Hanyang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mingchen, whose courtesy name was Kunchen, came from Hanyang in Hubei Province.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉土，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Daoguang (1835), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary academician, and was appointed revising compiler.

sentences.zh: 十八年，出為陝西興安知府。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he went out as prefect of Xing'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1838) he was posted as prefect of Xing'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 歷山西雁平道、江西鹽道、雲南按察使，湖南、甘肅、廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as intendant of Yanping in Shanxi, salt controller of Jiangxi, provincial judicial commissioner of Yunnan, and provincial treasurer of Hunan, Gansu, and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as intendant of the Yanping circuit in Shanxi, Jiangxi salt controller, Yunnan judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer of Hunan, Gansu, and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1848) he was promoted to governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，英人欲踐入城之約，名琛偕總督徐廣縉堅執勿許，聯合民團，嚴為戒備。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the English wished to fulfill the entry agreement; Mingchen together with Governor-General Xu Guangjin firmly refused permission, united the militia, and made strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, when the British sought to enforce the entry agreement, Mingchen joined Governor-General Xu Guangjin in a firm refusal, rallied the militia, and put the province on a war footing.

sentences.zh: 華商自停貿易以製之，英人始寢前議。

translations.literal: Chinese merchants on their own stopped trade to restrain them; the English then laid aside the former proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants imposed a trade boycott to pressure them, and the British finally dropped the demand.

sentences.zh: 論功，封一等男爵，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as a first-rank baron and granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was created a first-class baron and granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三十年，平英德土匪，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he pacified bandits in Yingde and received special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1850) he suppressed bandits in Yingde and received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，殲羅鏡會匪吳三，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he annihilated the Luojing secret-society bandit Wu San and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) he destroyed the Luojing rebel Wu San and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，廣縉赴廣西督師，命名琛接辦羅鏡剿捕事宜，出駐高州。

translations.literal: In the second year Guangjin went to Guangxi to command the army; Mingchen was ordered to take over the Luojing suppression and pursuit, and went out to station at Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Guangjin went to Guangxi to command the campaign, Mingchen was assigned the Luojing suppression and took the field from Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，羅鏡匪首凌十八就殲，加總督銜，署總督，赴南、韶一帶督剿。

translations.literal: That autumn the Luojing bandit chief Ling Shiba was destroyed; he was given governor-general rank, acted as governor-general, and went to the Nan and Shao regions to supervise suppression.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ling Shiba, the Luojing rebel chief, was destroyed; Mingchen received governor-general rank, served as acting governor-general, and took charge of operations in the Nanxiong and Shaozhou districts.

sentences.zh: 尋實授兩廣總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was substantively appointed governor-general of the two Guang provinces, concurrently superintendent of trade.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed full governor-general of the two Guang provinces and superintendent of foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 時廣東盜賊蜂起，四年，廣州群匪擾及省城，遣將分路進剿，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed in Guangdong; in the fourth year Guangzhou mob bandits disturbed even the provincial city; he dispatched generals on separate routes to attack, winning successive battles.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rampant in Guangdong; in the fourth year (1854) mobs threatened the provincial capital itself. He sent generals on several columns and won a string of victories.

sentences.zh: 近省之佛山、龍門、從化、東莞、陽山、河源、增城、封川，韶州之海豐、開建，潮州之惠來，肇慶府城及德慶並陷，先後克復。

translations.literal: Nearby Foshan, Longmen, Conghua, Dongguan, Yangshan, Heyuan, Zengcheng, Fengchuan, Haifeng and Kaijian of Shaozhou, Huilai of Chaozhou, the prefectural city of Zhaoqing and Deqing all fell and were recovered in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Foshan, Longmen, Conghua, Dongguan, Yangshan, Heyuan, Zengcheng, Fengchuan, Haifeng and Kaijian in Shaozhou, Huilai in Chaozhou, and the prefectural seats of Zhaoqing and Deqing all fell and were retaken in turn.

sentences.zh: 鄰省軍務方亟，糧餉器械多賴廣東接濟，名琛籌供無缺，益得時譽。

translations.literal: Neighboring provinces' military affairs were urgent; grain, funds, and weapons largely relied on Guangdong for support; Mingchen supplied without shortage and gained further contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring provinces were hard pressed in the war and depended heavily on Guangdong for grain, funds, and arms; Mingchen kept the supplies flowing and won still greater praise.

sentences.zh: 五年，以總督協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, as governor-general he was made assistant Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1855) he was made assistant Grand Secretary while retaining the governorship.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜體仁閣大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Birenjian Pavilion, still retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1856) he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Birenjian Pavilion while continuing as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 名琛性木彊，勤吏事，屬僚憚其威重。

translations.literal: Mingchen's nature was stubborn; he was diligent in official business, and subordinates feared his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen was stubborn by nature, tireless in administration, and his subordinates stood in awe of his authority.

sentences.zh: 初以偕徐廣縉拒英人入城被殊眷，因狃於前事，頗自負，好大言，遇中外交涉事，略書數字答之，或竟不答。

translations.literal: At first, because together with Xu Guangjin he had refused English entry into the city, he received exceptional favor; clinging to that past success he was quite self-confident, fond of grand words; encountering Sino-foreign affairs he would answer with a few characters or not answer at all.
translations.idiomatic: He had first won exceptional favor for joining Xu Guangjin in blocking British entry into Canton; resting on that success he grew arrogant, spoke in grand terms, and on foreign affairs would scribble a few lines in reply—or ignore the message altogether.

sentences.zh: 會匪之逼廣州，或議借外國兵禦賊者，斥之退。

translations.literal: When secret-society bandits pressed Guangzhou, some proposed borrowing foreign troops to repel the bandits; he rebuked them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels threatened Guangzhou, some suggested hiring foreign troops to help; he dismissed the idea out of hand.

sentences.zh: 匪既平，按察使沈棣輝功最多，列上官紳兵練出力者請獎，格不奏，兵練皆解體。

translations.literal: After the bandits were pacified, Provincial Judicial Commissioner Shen Dihui had the greatest merit; he listed officials, gentry, and militia who had exerted themselves and requested rewards, but the memorial was blocked and not submitted; the militia all disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, Judicial Commissioner Shen Dihui had done the most; Mingchen drew up a list of officials, gentry, and militia deserving reward but refused to submit it, and the militia drifted apart.

sentences.zh: 又嚴治通匪餘黨，或藉捕匪仇殺，從賊逃不敢歸，其黠者投香港，勸英人攻廣州。

translations.literal: He also strictly punished remnants who had communicated with bandits; some used bandit-hunting to settle private scores; those who had followed the bandits fled and dared not return; the cunning ones went to Hong Kong and urged the English to attack Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also cracked down harshly on those accused of aiding the rebels; some used the campaign as cover for private vendettas; former followers fled and dared not return, and the cleverest took refuge in Hong Kong and urged the British to attack Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會水師千總巡河，遇划艇張英國旗，搜獲十三人，拔其旗。

translations.literal: It happened that a naval patrol lieutenant was patrolling the river, met a rowboat flying the British flag, searched and seized thirteen men, and pulled down the flag.
translations.idiomatic: A naval patrol lieutenant on river duty came upon a rowboat flying the British flag, searched it, seized thirteen men, and tore down the flag.

sentences.zh: 英領事巴夏禮索之不得，貽書名​​琛責問，謂捕匪當移取，不當擅執，毀旗尤非禮。

translations.literal: British Consul Parkes could not recover them and sent a letter to Mingchen reproaching him, saying that in seizing bandits one should request transfer, not seize on one's own authority, and destroying the flag was especially discourteous.
translations.idiomatic: Consul Parkes could not get them back and wrote to Mingchen in protest, arguing that suspects should be handed over on request, not seized unilaterally, and that tearing down the flag was an insult.

sentences.zh: 名琛令送十三人於領事，不受，必欲並索千總，遂置之。

translations.literal: Mingchen ordered the thirteen men sent to the consul; they were not accepted; he insisted on also demanding the lieutenant, and the matter was left there.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen ordered the thirteen men delivered to the consulate; Parkes refused them and also demanded the lieutenant; Mingchen let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遣通事來告：「越日日中不如約，即攻城。」

translations.literal: Before long he sent an interpreter to announce: "If the agreement is not met by noon tomorrow, the city will be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: Soon an interpreter came with a warning: "If your terms are not met by noon tomorrow, we will attack the city."

sentences.zh: 至期，英兵果奪獵德、中流砲台。

translations.literal: When the day came, English troops indeed seized the Liede and Zhongliu batteries.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed hour British troops seized the Liede and Zhongliu forts.

sentences.zh: 名琛曰：「彼當自走。」

translations.literal: Mingchen said: "They will leave on their own."
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen said, "They will withdraw on their own."

sentences.zh: 令水師勿與戰，於是鳳皇山、海珠諸砲台皆被踞，發砲擊省城，十月朔，毀城，既入復出。

translations.literal: He ordered the navy not to fight; thereupon Fenghuang Hill, Haizhu, and other batteries were all occupied; they fired on the provincial city; on the first day of the tenth month they breached the wall, entered, and withdrew again.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the navy not to engage. The British then took Fenghuang Hill, Haizhu, and the other forts, shelled the city, and on the first day of the tenth month breached the wall, entered, and withdrew again.

sentences.zh: 遣廣州知府往詰用兵之故，英人曰：「兩國官不晤，情不親。

translations.literal: He sent the prefect of Guangzhou to demand the reason for using troops; the English said: "When officials of the two countries do not meet, feelings are not close.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the prefect of Guangzhou to ask why force had been used; the British replied, "When the officials of our two countries do not meet, there can be no mutual trust.

sentences.zh: 誤聽傳言，屢乖和好。

translations.literal: Misled by rumors, amity has repeatedly been broken.
translations.idiomatic: Misled by rumors, we have repeatedly fallen out.

sentences.zh: 請入城面議。」

translations.literal: They asked to enter the city for a face-to-face discussion."
translations.idiomatic: They asked to enter the city for a face-to-face meeting."

sentences.zh: 名琛勿許。

translations.literal: Mingchen would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen refused.

sentences.zh: 請於城外會議，亦不許。

translations.literal: They asked to confer outside the city; that too was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When they asked to meet outside the walls, he refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 兵練數万來援，怵敵火器，不能力戰。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of militia came to aid, but fearing the enemy's firearms they could not fight vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of militia came to help, but they feared the enemy's firearms and could not put up a real fight.

sentences.zh: 民憤甚，焚英、法、美三國居室，凡昔十三行皆燼。

translations.literal: Popular anger was intense; residences of the English, French, and Americans were burned, and all the former Thirteen Factories were reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Public fury ran high; mobs burned the quarters of the British, French, and Americans, and the old Thirteen Factories district was left in ashes.

sentences.zh: 英兵亦焚民居數千家，退泊大黃，各報其國。

translations.literal: English troops also burned several thousand civilian dwellings, withdrew and anchored at Whampoa, and each reported to his country.
translations.idiomatic: British troops burned thousands of civilian homes in return, withdrew to Whampoa, and each side reported home.

sentences.zh: 英遣額羅金來粵，聚兵澳門、香港，貽書索償款。

translations.literal: England sent Elgin to Guangdong, massed troops at Macao and Hong Kong, and sent letters demanding indemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Britain sent Lord Elgin to Canton, concentrated troops at Macao and Hong Kong, and demanded indemnities in writing.

sentences.zh: 名琛以其言狂悖，不答。

translations.literal: Mingchen considered his words arrogant and insolent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen judged his demands outrageous and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 法、美兩國領事亦索賠償，且告英兵已決計攻城，原居間排解。

translations.literal: The French and American consuls also demanded compensation, and moreover reported that English troops had decided to attack the city, offering originally to mediate and settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: The French and American consuls also demanded compensation and warned that British forces had resolved to storm the city, offering at first to mediate.

sentences.zh: 名琛慮其合以脅我，亦不聽；

translations.literal: Mingchen feared they would join to coerce China and would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen feared they would combine to coerce him and would not hear them out;

sentences.zh: 且不設備。

translations.literal: nor did he make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: nor did he make any preparations for defense.

sentences.zh: 七年，英兵攻東莞，總兵董開慶與戰，軍潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh year English troops attacked Dongguan; Regional Commander Dong Kaiqing fought them and the army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1857) British forces attacked Dongguan; Regional Commander Dong Kaiqing met them in battle and his army was routed.

sentences.zh: 額羅金遣艇遞照會，名琛答以通商而外，概不能從。

translations.literal: Elgin sent a boat to deliver a formal note; Mingchen replied that apart from trade, nothing else could be agreed to.
translations.idiomatic: Elgin sent a launch with an official note; Mingchen replied that beyond continuing trade he would agree to nothing.

sentences.zh: 累疏言：「英國主厭兵，粵事皆額羅金等所為。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized, saying: "The British sovereign is weary of war; the Guangdong affair is all the doing of Elgin and others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent repeated memorials claiming: "The British queen is weary of war; the trouble in Guangdong is entirely the work of Elgin and his party.

sentences.zh: 臣始終堅持，彼窮當自伏。」

translations.literal: Your servant has held firm throughout; when they are cornered they will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: I have held firm throughout; when they are cornered they will yield on their own."

sentences.zh: 密詔戒勿輕視，猶信其事有把握，仍褒勉之。

translations.literal: A secret edict warned against underestimating the enemy, yet still believed he had matters in hand and continued to praise and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict warned him not to underestimate the enemy, but the court still believed he had matters under control and continued to praise and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 九月，英兵驟至，法、美兵皆從。

translations.literal: In the ninth month English troops arrived suddenly; French and American troops all followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month British forces arrived without warning, with French and American troops following.

sentences.zh: 將軍司道商戰守，名琛惟恃通事張云同為內應，待敵窮蹙。

translations.literal: The general, provincial officials, and merchants discussed war and defense; Mingchen only relied on the interpreter Zhang Yuntong as an inside contact, waiting for the enemy to be cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Generals, provincial officials, and merchants debated war and defense, while Mingchen relied solely on his interpreter Zhang Yuntong as a go-between and waited for the enemy to collapse.

sentences.zh: 民間見其夷然不驚，事皆秘不宣示，轉疑其陽拒陰撫，人心益渙。

translations.literal: Among the people, seeing him utterly unalarmed and keeping everything secret without announcement, they came instead to suspect he was rejecting openly while appeasing in secret, and popular morale grew more scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The people saw him show no alarm and keep everything secret; they began to suspect he was defying the foreigners in public while appeasing them in private, and morale fell apart.

sentences.zh: 十一月，敵張榜城外，限二十四時破城，勸商民遷避。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the enemy posted proclamations outside the city, giving twenty-four hours to take the city and urging merchants and people to move away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the allies posted notices outside the walls, giving twenty-four hours before the city would fall and urging merchants and residents to flee.

sentences.zh: 砲擊總督署，延燒市廛，城遂陷。

translations.literal: They shelled the governor-general's yamen, the fire spread through the markets, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: They shelled the governor-general's compound, fire spread through the markets, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 巡撫柏貴檄紳士伍崇曜等議和，名琛猶持不許入城之議，夜避左都統署，英人大索得之，舁登舟。

translations.literal: Governor Bogui summoned gentry such as Wu Chongyao to discuss peace; Mingchen still held to the policy of forbidding entry into the city, fled by night to the Left Banner commander's office; the English searched widely and found him, and carried him aboard ship.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bogui summoned gentry including Wu Chongyao to negotiate peace; Mingchen still clung to his refusal of entry into the city, fled at night to a Manchu banner office, was hunted down by the British, and carried off to their ships.

sentences.zh: 將軍、巡撫以聞，詔斥名琛剛愎自用，辦理乖謬，褫其職，英人遂踞省城，禁巡撫等官不得出，責以安民。

translations.literal: The general and governor reported; an edict rebuked Mingchen for obstinacy and self-will, mishandling affairs; his office was stripped; the English then occupied the provincial city, forbade the governor and other officials to leave, and charged them with pacifying the people.
translations.idiomatic: The general and governor reported to the throne; an edict condemned Mingchen for stubbornness and gross mismanagement and stripped him of office. The British then held the provincial capital, confined Bogui and other officials inside, and ordered them to keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 民各集團練，設總局於佛山，相持數年。

translations.literal: The people each gathered militia, established a headquarters at Foshan, and the standoff lasted several years.
translations.idiomatic: The people organized militia companies and set up a headquarters at Foshan; the stalemate lasted several years.

sentences.zh: 各國聯師赴天津，事乃益棘矣。

translations.literal: The allied armies of various nations went to Tianjin, and matters grew still more acute.
translations.idiomatic: The allied powers then marched on Tianjin, and the crisis grew far worse.

sentences.zh: 名琛既被虜，英人挾至印度孟加拉，居之鎮海樓上。

translations.literal: After Mingchen was taken captive, the English carried him to Bengal in India and housed him in the Zhenhai Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mingchen was a prisoner, the British took him to Bengal in India and kept him in the Zhenhai Tower.

sentences.zh: 猶時作書畫，自署曰「海上蘇武」，賦詩見志，日誦呂祖經不輟。

translations.literal: He still sometimes made calligraphy and paintings, signing himself "Su Wu on the Sea," composing poetry to express his resolve, and daily reciting the Scripture of Patriarch Lü without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He still painted and wrote calligraphy, signing himself "Su Wu upon the sea," wrote poetry to declare his loyalty, and recited the scripture of Patriarch Lü every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，乃歸其屍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, and only then was his corpse returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1859) he died, and his body was sent home.

sentences.zh: 粵人憾其誤國，為之語曰：「不戰、不和、不守，不死、不降、不走；

translations.literal: The people of Guangdong resented that he had harmed the state and made a saying about him: "No fighting, no peace, no defense; no death, no surrender, no flight;
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese who blamed him for ruining the country composed a rhyme: "He would not fight, would not treat, would not defend; would not die, would not surrender, would not flee;

sentences.zh: 相臣度量，疆臣抱負；

translations.literal: the breadth of mind of a Grand Secretary, the ambition of a frontier minister;
translations.idiomatic: the magnanimity of a Grand Secretary, the resolve of a frontier governor;

sentences.zh: 古之所無，今之罕有。」

translations.literal: what antiquity never had, what the present rarely sees."
translations.idiomatic: unknown in antiquity, rarely seen today."

sentences.zh: 黃宗漢，字壽臣，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Huang Zonghan, courtesy name Shouchen, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zonghan, whose courtesy name was Shouchen, came from Jinjiang in Fujian Province.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi and was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of Daoguang (1835) and entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary academician.

sentences.zh: 散館改兵部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: After leaving the academy he was transferred to a principal clerk in the Ministry of War and served as a secretarial clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin training he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of War and served on the staff of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎、郎中，遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice director and director, and was promoted to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks as vice director and director, then became a censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，出為廣東督糧道，調雷瓊道，歷山東、浙江按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as grain transport commissioner of Guangdong, was transferred to the Lei-Qiong circuit, and successively served as provincial judicial commissioner of Shandong and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1845) he was posted as Guangdong grain transport commissioner, transferred to the Leizhou and Qiongzhou circuit, and later served as judicial commissioner of Shandong and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，巡撫吳文鎔薦宗漢可重用，遷甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, Governor Wu Wenrong recommended Zonghan as fit for important use; he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Governor Wu Wenrong recommended Zonghan for higher responsibility, and he was appointed provincial treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢雲南巡撫，未之任，調浙江。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan, did not take up the post, and was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1852) he was promoted to governor of Yunnan but never took up the post and was transferred to Zhejiang instead.

sentences.zh: 值試辦海運，湖郡漕船淺滯，改留變價，虧銀三十餘萬兩，布政使椿壽情急自縊。

translations.literal: It happened that trial sea transport was being undertaken; grain boats of the lake districts ran aground in shallow water, were detained and sold off, with a loss of more than three hundred thousand taels of silver; Provincial Treasurer Chunshou, in distress, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: While a trial of grain transport by sea was under way, tribute boats on the lake routes ran aground; the grain was sold locally at a loss of more than three hundred thousand taels, and Provincial Treasurer Chunshou hanged himself in despair.

sentences.zh: 宗漢疏請原米隨新漕運京，允之。

translations.literal: Zonghan memorialized requesting that the original grain be sent to the capital with the new tribute transport; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan memorialized that the stranded grain should be forwarded to Beijing with the new tribute shipment, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪犯江寧，調浙江兵二千名赴援。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangdong rebels attacked Jiangning; two thousand Zhejiang troops were transferred to aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1853), when Guangdong rebels threatened Nanjing, he sent two thousand Zhejiang troops to help defend the city.

sentences.zh: 江寧尋陷，宗漢赴嘉興、湖州籌防，疏言不可僅於本境畫疆而守。

translations.literal: Jiangning soon fell; Zonghan went to Jiaxing and Huzhou to organize defense, memorializing that one must not merely guard within one's own boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing soon fell; Zonghan went to Jiaxing and Huzhou to organize defenses and argued in a memorial that Zhejiang could not simply defend its own borders.

sentences.zh: 於是分兵赴江蘇、安徽境內協防，詔嘉其妥協。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided troops to assist in defense within Jiangsu and Anhui; an edict praised his well-judged arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent troops into Jiangsu and Anhui to help hold the line, and the court praised his sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 尋上海匪起陷城，請海運改於劉河受兌。

translations.literal: Soon rebels rose in Shanghai and took the city; he requested that sea transport be changed to receive tribute at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized Shanghai, he asked that the sea transport route be shifted to Liuhe for collection of tribute grain.

sentences.zh: 時江南大營需餉甚鉅，宗漢貽書向榮，通盤籌算，請於江蘇、浙江、江西三省確定每月額數。

translations.literal: At the time the great camp in Jiangnan needed funds in huge amounts; Zonghan wrote to Xiang Rong, planning comprehensively, requesting that fixed monthly quotas be set for Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The great Jiangnan camp needed vast supplies; Zonghan wrote to Xiang Rong with a comprehensive plan to fix monthly quotas from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 榮據以上聞，文宗韙之。

translations.literal: Xiang reported upward; the Wenzong Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang forwarded the plan to the throne, and the Xianfeng Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 四年，特詔褒宗漢辦理防務、海運，及本境治匪、察吏，精詳無瞻顧，深堪嘉尚，特賜御書「忠勤正直」扁額，勉其慎終如始，以成一代良臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year a special edict praised Zonghan for handling defense, sea transport, and within his jurisdiction suppressing bandits and inspecting officials, with meticulous care and no hesitation, deeply worthy of commendation; he was specially granted an imperial inscription plaque reading "Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Straightforward," exhorted to be careful to the end as at the beginning and become a worthy minister of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1854) a special edict praised Zonghan for his defense work, sea transport, suppression of bandits, and inspection of officials—praising his thoroughness and courage—and granted him an imperial plaque inscribed "Loyal, diligent, upright, and straight," urging him to finish as he had begun and become a minister worthy of his age.

sentences.zh: 擢四川總督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 給事中張修育疏言：「宗漢治浙，佈置合宜，未可更易。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Xiuyu memorialized, saying: "Zonghan's governance of Zhejiang is well arranged and should not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Xiuyu memorialized: "Zonghan's administration of Zhejiang is soundly arranged and he should not be moved."

sentences.zh: 詔不允。

translations.literal: An edict did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 會因數月未奏事，降旨詢問，以疾為言，詔斥之，議降三級調用，加恩降二品頂戴，​​仍留總督任。

translations.literal: It happened that for several months he had not memorialized; an edict was issued to inquire; he pleaded illness; an edict rebuked him; demotion by three ranks and transfer was proposed; grace reduced it to second-rank button and he still retained the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When he failed to report for several months, the throne inquired; he pleaded illness and was rebuked; demotion by three ranks was proposed, but as a favor he was allowed to keep second-rank insignia and remain in the Sichuan post.

sentences.zh: 五年，馬邊夷匪為亂，平之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Yi bandits at Mabian rebelled; he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1855) tribal rebels rose at Mabian on the Sichuan frontier; he suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 遵旨遣松潘鎮總兵德恩以兵二千援荊州，又調兵四千赴貴州剿苗，並協餉十萬兩。

translations.literal: Following an edict he sent Regional Commander De'en of Songpan with two thousand troops to aid Jingzhou, and also transferred four thousand troops to Guizhou to suppress Miao rebels, together contributing one hundred thousand taels of funds.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial orders he sent Regional Commander De'en of Songpan with two thousand men to relieve Jingzhou, dispatched four thousand troops to Guizhou against the Miao rebels, and contributed one hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 六年，復因久無奏報，命將軍樂斌查奏，以痰疾聞，下部議降調，命來京另候簡用。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, again because of long absence of memorials, General Leqin was ordered to investigate and report; phlegm illness was reported; the ministry proposed demotion and transfer; he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1856), again for long silence in reporting, General Leqin was ordered to investigate; Zonghan cited phlegm illness; the ministry proposed demotion; he was recalled to Beijing to await a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 補內閣學士，兼署刑部侍郎、順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Grand Secretariat academician, concurrently acting as vice minister of justice and governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Grand Secretariat academician and concurrently served as vice minister of justice and governor of the capital prefecture of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 廣東軍事起，葉名琛被擄，授宗漢兩廣總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: When military affairs arose in Guangdong and Ye Mingchen was captured, Zonghan was appointed governor-general of the two Guang provinces, concurrently superintendent of trade.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Guangdong and Ye Mingchen was taken prisoner, Zonghan was appointed governor-general of the two Guang provinces and superintendent of foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 時廣州為英人所踞，巡撫柏貴在城中為所脅制。

translations.literal: At the time Guangzhou was occupied by the English; Governor Bogui in the city was coerced by them.
translations.idiomatic: Canton was then in British hands, and Governor Bogui inside the city was under their control.

sentences.zh: 民團四起，文宗因徐廣縉等前拒英人入城，賴紳民之力，欲復用之，命在籍侍郎羅惇衍、京卿龍元僖、給事中蘇廷魁治團練。

translations.literal: Militia rose everywhere; the Wenzong Emperor, because Xu Guangjin and others had formerly refused English entry into the city and relied on the power of gentry and people, wished to use them again, and ordered retired Grand Secretary Luo Dunyi, capital official Long Yuanxi, and Supervising Secretary Su Tingkui to manage the militia.
translations.idiomatic: Militia sprang up everywhere; recalling how Xu Guangjin had blocked British entry with gentry and commoners behind him, the Xianfeng Emperor wanted to revive that strategy and ordered retired officials Luo Dunyi, Long Yuanxi, and Su Tingkui to organize the militia.

sentences.zh: 惇衍等號召鄉團，得數万人，戒期攻城，卒無功；

translations.literal: Dunyi and others summoned village militia, mustering tens of thousands, set a date to attack the city, but in the end achieved nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Dunyi and the others raised village militia numbering tens of thousands, fixed a date to storm the city, and failed;

sentences.zh: 又禁華人不得受僱為洋人服役以困之。

translations.literal: they also forbade Chinese from being hired to serve foreigners in order to distress them.
translations.idiomatic: they also forbade Chinese from working for foreigners in order to pressure them.

sentences.zh: 八年春，各國遣人赴江蘇投書致京師大學士訴粵事，請遣大臣至上海會議；

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year various nations sent men to Jiangsu to deliver letters to Grand Secretaries in the capital complaining of Guangdong affairs, requesting that a high minister be sent to Shanghai for negotiations;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year (1858) the foreign powers sent envoys to Jiangsu with letters to Grand Secretaries in Beijing about the Canton crisis, asking that a senior minister come to Shanghai for talks;

sentences.zh: 且言逾期即赴天津。

translations.literal: and said that if the deadline passed they would go to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: and threatening to proceed to Tianjin if the deadline passed.

sentences.zh: 詔仍回廣東候宗漢查辦，而英、俄兩國兵船已泊吳淞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them still to return to Guangdong to await Zonghan's investigation and handling, but English and Russian warships had already anchored at Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the envoys back to Guangdong to await Zonghan's investigation, but British and Russian warships were already at Wusong.

sentences.zh: 宗漢過江蘇，總督何桂清堅留在上海開議，宗漢不可，遽去；

translations.literal: Zonghan passed through Jiangsu; Governor He Guiqing firmly urged him to stay and open negotiations at Shanghai; Zonghan would not agree and hurried away;
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan passed through Jiangsu; Governor He Guiqing pressed him to stay in Shanghai for negotiations, but Zonghan refused and hurried on;

sentences.zh: 取道浙、閩，調兵不可得。

translations.literal: taking the route through Zhejiang and Fujian, he could not obtain transferred troops.
translations.idiomatic: traveling through Zhejiang and Fujian, he could raise no troops.

sentences.zh: 及至廣東，敵兵已犯天津。

translations.literal: When he reached Guangdong, enemy troops had already attacked Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Guangdong, the allied forces had already struck Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 宗漢駐惠州，惟恃聯絡民團，出示空言激勵，為英人所禁格，不能遍及。

translations.literal: Zonghan stationed at Huizhou, relying only on linking with militia, issuing empty words to encourage them; the English blocked and obstructed this so it could not spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan stayed at Huizhou, relying only on links with local militia and empty proclamations to rouse them; the British blocked such messages from circulating widely.

sentences.zh: 既而天津和約成，俟償款六百萬兩分年交畢，始退出廣州，粵民愈憤。

translations.literal: Soon the Tianjin treaty was concluded; only after six million taels of indemnity were paid in installments over years did they withdraw from Guangzhou; the people of Guangdong grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Treaty of Tianjin was signed, the allies agreed to leave Canton only after six million taels of indemnity had been paid in installments; the Cantonese grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 英領事宣布和議，新安鎮鄉勇殺其張示者數人，遂發兵陷新安。

translations.literal: The English consul proclaimed the peace agreement; militia of Xin'an Town killed several of those who posted the notices, and troops were then sent to take Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the British consul posted the peace terms, militia from Xin'an Town killed several men who put up the notices, and British troops seized the town in retaliation.

sentences.zh: 民團大舉攻城，初勝終挫，懸賞格購洋官首，亦僅時伺隱僻，有所殺傷而已。

translations.literal: Militia launched a major attack on the city, winning at first but defeated in the end; rewards were posted to buy foreign officers' heads, but only occasionally in hidden places were some killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Militia mounted a major assault on the city, winning early fights but losing in the end; rewards were offered for foreign officers' heads, but only a few were killed in ambushes here and there.

sentences.zh: 宗漢外怵強敵，內畏民嵒，不能有所措施。

translations.literal: Zonghan outwardly feared the strong enemy, inwardly feared the wrath of the people, and could take no measures.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan feared the foreign enemy abroad and popular fury at home, and could devise no effective policy.

sentences.zh: 泊大學士桂良等至上海議稅則及換約事宜，將與商交還廣州，向宗漢詢近狀，輒不答。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Guiliang and others reached Shanghai to negotiate tariff rates and treaty revision, about to discuss return of Guangzhou with merchants, they inquired of Zonghan about recent conditions, but he repeatedly did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Guiliang reached Shanghai to negotiate tariffs and treaty revision and to discuss the return of Canton, he asked Zonghan for reports on the situation, but Zonghan would not reply.

sentences.zh: 而英人以既議和，民團復相仇殺，來相詰問，且揭團紳告示載諭旨有異，必欲去宗漢及三團紳。

translations.literal: But the English, because peace had been negotiated yet militia again killed one another, came to press for answers, and moreover exposed militia gentry proclamations whose recorded edicts differed, insisting on removing Zonghan and the three militia gentry leaders.
translations.idiomatic: The British, noting that fighting continued among militia even after peace talks, pressed for explanations and produced militia proclamations bearing edicts that did not match the court's texts, demanding the removal of Zonghan and the three militia leaders.

sentences.zh: 桂良等疏聞，詔責宗漢捕偽造諭旨之人，罷其通商大臣，改授何桂清。

translations.literal: Guiliang and others memorialized; an edict charged Zonghan to arrest those who forged edicts, removed him as superintendent of trade, and transferred the post to He Guiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Guiliang reported to the throne; an edict ordered Zonghan to arrest those who forged imperial edicts, stripped him of the trade superintendency, and gave the post to He Guiqing.

sentences.zh: 英使額羅金猶不愜，遽率監赴廣東。

translations.literal: English envoy Elgin was still not satisfied and abruptly led his staff to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Elgin was still not satisfied and abruptly led his staff back to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 九年，遂復有天津之役。

translations.literal: In the ninth year there was again the Tianjin campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1859) the allies struck Tianjin again.

sentences.zh: 尋調宗漢四川總督，召至京，改以侍郎候補。

translations.literal: Soon Zonghan was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan, summoned to the capital, and changed to await appointment as vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Sichuan as governor-general, recalled to Beijing, and reduced to await appointment as a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 十年，署吏部侍郎，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he acted as vice minister of personnel; soon substantively appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1860) he served as acting vice minister of personnel and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 四川京官呈請飭赴四川督辦團練，不許。

translations.literal: Beijing officials from Sichuan petitioned ordering him to go to Sichuan to supervise militia organization; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan officials in Beijing petitioned that he be sent home to organize militia; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 宗漢與載垣、端華、肅順等交結。

translations.literal: Zonghan associated with Zaiyuan, Duanhua, Sushun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was allied with Zaiyuan, Duanhua, Sushun, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，載垣等獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; Zaiyuan and others were punished for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861) the Tongzhi Emperor ascended the throne, and Zaiyuan and his associates were condemned.

sentences.zh: 少詹事許彭壽疏劾宗漢與陳孚恩、劉昆並黨肅順等，踪跡最密。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Xu Pengshou memorialized impeaching Zonghan together with Chen Fu'en and Liu Kun as all partisans of Sushun and others, their tracks most intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Xu Pengshou impeached Zonghan along with Chen Fu'en and Liu Kun as close associates of Sushun's faction.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「黃宗漢本年春赴熱河，危詞力阻回鑾。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Huang Zonghan this spring went to Rehe and with alarming words strongly obstructed the return of the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Huang Zonghan went to Rehe this spring and used alarmist language to block the emperor's return to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 迨皇考梓宮將回京，又以京城可慮，遍告於人，希冀阻止。

translations.literal: When Our late father's coffin was about to return to the capital, he again said the capital was to be feared, telling everyone widely, hoping to obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: When Our late father's coffin was about to return to the capital, he spread word that the city was unsafe, telling everyone he could in hopes of stopping the move.

sentences.zh: 其意存迎合載垣等，眾所共知。

translations.literal: His intention was to curry favor with Zaiyuan and others, as all know.
translations.idiomatic: His aim was plainly to curry favor with Zaiyuan and his party, as everyone knew.

sentences.zh: 聲名品行如此，若任其濫廁卿貳，何以表率屬僚？

translations.literal: With reputation and conduct such as this, if he is allowed to fill high offices at random, how can he set an example for subordinates?
translations.idiomatic: With a reputation and conduct such as this, how can he be allowed to hold high office and set an example for other officials?

sentences.zh: 革職永不敘用，以為大僚輭媚者戒。」

translations.literal: Strip office and never employ again, to warn high officials who are soft and fawning."
translations.idiomatic: Strip him of office and never employ him again, as a warning to high officials who cringe before power."

sentences.zh: 並追奪前賜御書「忠勤正直」扁額。

translations.literal: And the previously granted imperial inscription plaque "Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Straightforward" was also posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: The court also revoked the imperial plaque "Loyal, diligent, upright, and straight" that had been granted earlier.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tongzhi (1864).

sentences.zh: 論曰：當道、咸之間，海禁大開，然昧於外情，朝野一也。

translations.literal: The critique says: Between the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns the maritime prohibition was greatly opened, yet ignorant of foreign conditions, court and people were alike.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the Daoguang and Xianfeng eras the maritime frontier was thrown open, yet court and country alike were blind to foreign realities.

sentences.zh: 粵民身創夷患之深，目擊國威之墮，憤懼交乘，遂因拒入城一事，釀成大釁。

translations.literal: The people of Guangdong had personally suffered the depth of barbarian harm, witnessed the fall of national prestige; anger and fear combined, and thus from the matter of refusing entry into the city a great conflict was brewed.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese who had suffered deeply from foreign aggression and watched national prestige collapse were torn between anger and fear; the refusal to let foreigners into the city thus ignited a far greater crisis.

sentences.zh: 朝廷誤信民氣可用，而不知虛聲之不足恃也。

translations.literal: The court mistakenly believed popular spirit could be used, not knowing that empty reputation was not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The court wrongly believed popular fervor could be harnessed, not understanding that bluster alone could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 徐廣縉操縱有術，幸安一時；

translations.literal: Xu Guangjin had skill in manipulation and was fortunate to secure peace for a time;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangjin knew how to manage the situation and secured a temporary peace;

sentences.zh: 葉名琛狃於前事，驕愎致敗，宜哉。

translations.literal: Ye Mingchen clung to past affairs, arrogance and obstinacy brought defeat—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mingchen rested on his earlier success, and arrogance and obstinacy brought him down—as he deserved.

sentences.zh: 黃宗漢依違貽誤，終以依附權要被譴。

translations.literal: Huang Zonghan's wavering caused harm and delay, and in the end he was punished for clinging to powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zonghan's vacillation caused harm, and in the end he was punished for siding with the ruling clique.

sentences.zh: 廣縉在粵東剿平羅鏡匪有功，及代賽尚阿督師，軍事已壞，旁皇失措，咎無可辭焉。

translations.literal: Guangjin had merit in suppressing the Luojing bandits in eastern Guangdong; when he replaced Saišangga to command the army, military affairs were already ruined, he was flustered and at a loss, and blame cannot be excused.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin earned credit for suppressing the Luojing rebels in eastern Guangdong, but when he replaced Saišangga in command the war was already lost; his panic and indecision left him with no excuse.
